  All agenda items and reports are available for review in the City Clerk’s Office and
  www.hpca.gov. Any writings or documents provided to a majority of the City Council regarding
  any item on this agenda (other than writings legally exempt from public disclosure) will be
  made available for public inspection in the Office of the City Clerk located at 6550 Miles
  Avenue, Huntington Park, California 90255 during regular business hours, 7:00 a.m. to 5:30
  p.m., Monday – Thursday, and at the City Hall Council Chambers during the meeting.

  Any person who requires a disability-related modification or accommodation, including
  auxiliary aids or services, in order to participate in the public meeting may request such
  modification, accommodation, aid or service by contacting the City Clerk’s Office either in
  person at 6550 Miles Avenue, Huntington Park, California or by telephone at (323) 584-6230.
  Notification in advance of the meeting will enable the City to make reasonable arrangements
  to ensure accessibility to this meeting.

  PLEASE SILENCE ALL CELL PHONES AND OTHER ELECTRONIC

 PLEASE NOTE--The numerical order of items on this agenda is for convenience of reference.
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING AGENDA
April 16, 2024  Page 1 of 7
 Items may be taken out of order upon request of the Mayor or Members of the City Council.
Members of the City Council and the public are reminded that they must preserve order and
decorum throughout the Meeting. In that regard, Members of the City Council and the public
are advised that any delay or disruption in the proceedings or a refusal to obey the orders of
the City Council or the presiding officer constitutes a violation of these rules.

  •  The conduct of City Council meetings is governed by the portion of the California
  Government Code commonly known as the "Brown Act" and by the Huntington Park
  City Council Meeting Rules of Procedure.

  •  The City Council meeting is for conducting the City's business, and members of the
  audience must obey the rules of decorum set forth by law. This means that each
  speaker will be permitted to speak for three minutes to address items that are listed
  on the City Council agenda or topics which are within the jurisdictional authority of the
  City.

  •  No profanity, personal attacks, booing, cheering, applauding or other conduct
  disruptive to the meeting will be permitted. Any person not adhering to the Rules of
  Procedure or conduct authorized by the Brown Act may be asked to leave the Council
  Chambers.

  •  All comments directed to the City Council or to any member of the City Council must
  be directed to the Mayor (or Chairperson if Mayor is absent).

We ask that you please respect the business nature of this meeting and the order required
for the proceedings conducted in the Council Chambers.

PUBLIC COMMENT

For both open and closed session, each speaker will be limited to three minutes per
Huntington Park Municipal Code Section 2-1.207. Time limits may not be shared with other
speakers and may not accumulate from one period of public comment to another or from one
meeting to another. This is the only opportunity for public input except for scheduled
public hearing items.

All comments or queries shall be addressed to the Council as a body and not to any specific
member thereof. Pursuant to Government Code Section 54954.2(a)(2), the Ralph M. Brown
Act, no action or discussion by the City Council shall be undertaken on any item not appearing
on the posted agenda, except to briefly provide information, ask for clarification, provide
direction to staff, or schedule a matter for a future meeting.
ADDITIONS/DELETIONS TO AGENDA

Items of business may be added to the agenda upon a motion adopted by a minimum two-
thirds vote finding that there is a need to take immediate action and that the need for action
came to the attention of the City or Agency subsequent to the agenda being posted. Items
may be deleted from the agenda upon the request of staff or Council.

IMPORTANT NOTICE
The City of Huntington Park shows replays of City Council Meetings on Local Access
Channel 3 and over the Internet at www.hpca.gov. NOTE: Your attendance at this public
meeting may result in the recording and broadcast of your image and/or voice.

MINUTES
  Meeting of the
  City of Huntington Park City Council
  Tuesday, April 16, 2024

The regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Huntington Park, California was
called to order at 6:00 p.m. on Tuesday, April 16, 2024, in the Council Chambers at City
Hall, 6550 Miles Avenue, Huntington Park, California; Mayor Marilyn Sanabria presiding.

PRESENT: Council Member(s): Graciela Ortiz, Eduardo “Eddie” Martinez, Arturo Flores,
Vice Mayor Karina Macias and Mayor Sanabria

ABSENT:  None

CITY OFFICIALS/STAFF: City Manager Ricardo Reyes; Eduardo Sarmiento, City Clerk;
Cosme Lozano Police Chief; Steve Foster Director of Community Development; Sergio
Infanzon Director of Communications; Cynthia Norzagaray Director of Parks and Recreation;
Araceli Almazan City Attorney.

INVOCATION
Mayor Sanabria led the invocation.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE
Council member Flores led the Pledge of Allegiance.

PRESENTATION(S)
 1. 7TH ANNUAL HIPIAM COMMUNITY HEALTH FAIR STUDENT PRESENTATION
 2. CERTIFICATES OF RECOGNITION AND APPRECIATION FOR THE 5K
  EXHIBITORS AND SPONSORS
 3. CERTIFICATES OF APPRECIATION TO THE STATE OF THE CITY
  PARTICIPANTS

PUBLIC COMMENTS

The following persons provided public comment:
1. Lieutenant Gizar
2. Officer Hassan Saleh
3. Baldomero Capiz

STAFF RESPONSE

City Manager Ricardo Reyes provided information related to measure PP and what is to
come from its passing.

CLOSED SESSION
1. CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL – ANTICIPATED LITIGATION
  Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(1)
  Los Angeles Superior Court Case NO. 20STCPO3947
  Construction Industry Force Account Council v. City of Huntington Park

2. Angela Flores Romero v. HP 20STCV18416

Attorney Araceli Almazan stated that it is appropriate to recess to closed
session. Mayor Sanabria recessed into closed session at 6:40 p.m.

Mayor Sanabria reconvened the Council meeting from Closed Session at 7:05 p.m.

CLOSED SESSION ANNOUNCEMENT
City Attorney Almazan reported that the record should reflect that with all five (5)
members of the City Council present the two (2) items on the closed session agenda
were discussed. Regarding item one (1), Council was briefed but not further action was
taken. Regarding item two (2) on the closed session agenda, the City Council was briefed
and direction was provided. This concluded the closed session report.
   CONSENT CALENDAR
CITY CLERK

  MOTION: Council member Flores moved to approve the consent calendar,
  seconded by Vice Mayor Macias. Motion carried by unanimous consent.

  AYES:  Council Member(s): Ortiz, Martinez, Flores, Vice Mayor Macias
  and Mayor Sanabria

  NOES:  None

  MOTION: Council member Flores moved to adopt a Resolution approving the Urban
  Forestry and Fire Protection’s Urban Forestry Program, seconded by Council
  member Ortiz. Motion carried by unanimous consent.

  AYES:  Council Member(s): Ortiz, Martinez, Flores, Vice Mayor Macias
  and Mayor Sanabria

  NOES:  None

4.  APPROVAL ACCEPTANCE OF WORK PERFORMED FOR THE CIP 2018-11
  ACTIVE TRANSPORTATION PROGRAM CYCLE IV PROJECT NO. ATPL-5150
  (014)

  MOTION: Council member Ortiz moved to approve acceptance of work performed
  by Palp Inc. DBA Excel Paving for the construction of CIP 2018-11 Active
  Transportation Program Cycle 4 Project No. ATPL-5150(014); and authorize staff to
  execute the Notice of Completion (NOC) and direct the City Clerk to file the NOC
  with the Los Angeles County Recorder’s Office; and release the retention amount of
  $211,799.04 to Palp Inc. DBA Excel Paving 35 days after the effective date of the
  recordation of the NOC, if no Stop Notices are filed within the 35-day period,
  seconded by Council member Flores. Motion carried by unanimous consent.

  AYES:  Council Member(s): Ortiz, Martinez, Flores, Vice Mayor Macias
  and Mayor Sanabria

  NOES:  None

FINANCE

   MOTION: Council member Ortiz moved to receive and file the FY 2022 Audited
  Financial Statement, seconded by Vice Mayor Macias. Motion carried by unanimous

  AYES:  Council Member(s): Ortiz, Martinez, Flores, Vice Mayor Macias

  Motion carried by unanimous consent.

  AYES:  Council Member(s): Ortiz, Martinez, Flores, Vice Mayor Macias
  and Mayor Sanabria

  NOES:  None

  COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT BLOCK GRANT (CDBG) FUNDS FOR A CITY
  TUTORING PROGRAM

  MOTION: Council member Ortiz moved to adopt a resolution authorizing the
  expenditure of CDBG funds for a city tutoring program, seconded by Council member

  AYES:  Council Member(s): Ortiz, Martinez, Flores, Vice Mayor Macias
  and Mayor Sanabria

  NOES:  None

10.  COSNIDERATION OF A RESOLUTION AUTHORIZING THE EXPENDITURE OF
  FUNDS FOR A CITY SPAY AND NEUTER PROGRAM

  Item ten (10) was moved to the April 18, 2024 City Council meeting.
 11.  CONSIDERATION OF A RESOLUTION AUTHORIZING THE EXEPENDITURE OF
  FUNDS FOR A CITY LITERCY PROGRAM

  Item eleven (11) was moved to the April 18, 2024 City Council meeting.

  END OF REGULAR AGENDA

DEPARTMENTAL REPORTS

Community Development Director Steve Forster announced that well 15 is now up and
running. He gave a special thanks to Inframark staff including Rick Barba for their diligent
work.

Communications Department Director Sergion Infanzon provided information on
upcoming city events like Earth Day and the Annual Art Walk. He encouraged all
residents to visit the city website for additional information.

WRITTEN COMMUNICATIONS

None

COUNCIL COMMUNICATIONS
Council member Ortiz thanked all departments and staff for their hard work. She shared
her gratitude for supporting her vision to improve the city and its programing throughout
her tenure as a city council member.

Council member Matinez thanked staff for providing a safe space to meet. He then
shared how it has been a pleasure working with both Council member Ortiz and Mayor
Sanabria. He added that they have been great representatives for woman and all the
residents of Huntington Park. He then shared information about the upcoming
community clean up event and encouraged everyone to participate. He closed by
reminding residents to bring out any bulky items on Friday evening to have those items
collected Saturday.

Council member Flores acknowledged the Finance Department for their hard work with
the audits. He also shared his enthusiasm regarding the water wells and the great
progress that is being made.

Vice Mayor Macias thanked staff for their hard work for the community. She then shared
her appreciation for the outgoing Mayor Sanabria and Council member Ortiz and
thanked them for their commitment to the Huntington Park community and all they
achieved.

Mayor Sanabria thanked staff for their hard work with the water wells and all the other
city projects they have helped bring to fruition.

ADJOURNMENT

MOTION: Council member Flores moved to adjourn the meeting in honor of her
grandmother Rosa Arevalo to a Regular meeting on Tuesday May 7, 2024. The meeting
adjourned at 7:25pm.
 Respectfully submitted

Eduardo Sarmiento, City Clerk
